## Cornwall National Landscape

Cornwall National Landscape is unique, it is the only National Landscape that has 12 separate sections totalling almost a third of Cornwall, 958 sq. km (370 square miles). Cornwall is a beautiful part of the world, with a world-renowned coastline, a UNESCO World Heritage Site designation, and a host of natural and heritage features.

![Cornwall map](https://national-landscapes.transforms.svdcdn.com/production/assets/images/Maps/cornwall_map.png?w=300&auto=compress%2Cformat&fit=crop&dm=1700483314&s=2580f37bd6ee5c021e78c86181deec7f)

[Visit website](https://cornwall-landscape.org/)

We areCornwallNational Landscape

![](https://i.ytimg.com/vi/TrnjAL7ZFxE/maxresdefault.jpg)Play video: Introduction video

Cornwall National Landscape is the new name for the protected landscape in Cornwall, endorsed by Natural England. We are still in law a designated area of outstanding natural beauty (AONB). Cornwall National Landscape is 12 separate sections making up one third of Cornwall and our primary purpose remains to conserve and enhance Natural Beauty.

Cornwall is a beautiful part of the world, with a world-renowned coastline, a UNESCO World Heritage Site designation, and a host of natural and heritage features that make it unique and such a draw for visitors and residents alike. National Landscapes are protected landscapes whose distinctive character and natural beauty are so outstanding that it is in the nation’s interest to safeguard them. As such they have been nationally designated by the same legislation as National Parks and have the same status and level of protection.

Cornwall National Landscape is unique, it is the only protected landscape that has 12 separate sections totalling almost a third of Cornwall – an area bigger than Dartmoor National Park.

## It's all part of the plan

A shared strategy for those who live, work and visit the Cornwall National Landscape. It provides guidance to help Government, statutory organisations and any public body to ensure they are fulfilling their Section 85\* duty to ‘have regard to the purpose of conserving and enhancing the natural beauty’ of the protected landscape.

[Download PDF](https://cnl-image-store.storage.googleapis.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/17151258/plan-fixed-and-wheel-XS.pdf) [The Management Plan hub](https://cornwall-landscape.org/about-cornwall-national-landscapes/the-management-plan/)

### Cornwall National Landscape: An Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty Management Plan Review 2025-27

The Cornwall National Landscape: An Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty Management Plan is a statutory plan. It is Cornwall Council’s duty under the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000 to produce the Management Plan and review it every five years. The Management Plan sets out the policies and strategy by which the National Landscape should be managed.

[Have your say](https://letstalk.cornwall.gov.uk/cornwall-national-landscape)

![Cornwall National Landscape: An Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty Management Plan Review 2025-27](https://cnl-image-store.storage.googleapis.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/03111515/St-Gennys-Cliff-Castle_aerials-11-1024x767.jpg)
St Gennys Cliff Castle

### Forces for Change

We are designated to conserve and enhance natural beauty, but we face significant pressures that drive landscape change. These forces are a mixture of environmental, social, economic, and policy-driven factors that alter the character, biodiversity, and community structure of these protected areas.

[Forces for Change](https://cornwall-landscape.org/about-cornwall-national-landscapes/the-management-plan/forces-for-change/)

![Forces for Change](https://cnl-image-store.storage.googleapis.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/17151316/Area-6-Waterfront-at-Devoran-Barry-Gamble-1024x683.jpg)
Area 6 Waterfront at Devoran, Barry Gamble, courtesy of Cornwall Mining World Heritage Site

### The Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000

The Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000 (CRoW) subsumes and strengthens the AONB provisions of the 1949 Act. It confirms the purpose and significance of AONBs, clarifies the procedure for their designation, and created a firm legislative basis for their designation, protection and management.

[The Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000 (CRoW)](https://cornwall-landscape.org/about-cornwall-national-landscapes/the-management-plan/the-countryside-and-rights-of-way-act-2000-crow/)

![The Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000](https://cnl-image-store.storage.googleapis.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/26133216/Gunwalloe-storm-Caroline-Pack-768x1024.jpg)
Gunwalloe storm – Caroline Pack

### Our Policies aim and objectives

The Strategy for Cornwall AONB is underpinned by four priorities: People, Place, Nature and Climate as well as local AONB aims, policies and objectives which page will outline in detail.

[Cornwall AONB Aims,Policies and Objectives](https://cornwall-landscape.org/about-cornwall-national-landscapes/the-management-plan/cornwall-aonb-aimspolicies-and-objectives/)

![Our Policies aim and objectives](https://cnl-image-store.storage.googleapis.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/10/17151423/55-Porthleven-Pier-in-morn-empty-during-Covid-lockdown-Matt-Menhenett.jpg)
Porthleven Pier in morning empty during Covid lockdown – Matt Menhenett

## Our priorities

Our primary purpose is to conserve and enhance Natural Beauty.

Our priority is to lead and support projects which deliver under these four key priorities.

[Find Out More](https://cornwall-landscape.org/cornwall-national-landscape-priorities/)

![People](https://cornwall-landscape.org/wp-content/themes/aonb/resources/images/people.svg)

### People

Communities in the Cornwall National Landscape live entirely outside the main towns, within villages, hamlets and scattered farmsteads, dispersed throughout the landscape. It’s a mixed picture with areas of extreme wealth and also extreme deprivation.

[Read more](https://cornwall-landscape.org/cornwall-national-landscape-priorities/7257-2/)

![Place](https://cornwall-landscape.org/wp-content/themes/aonb/resources/images/place.svg)

### Place

The beauty of the landscape is primarily owed to the stewardship of generations of farmers and landowners. It is essential to understand and value its diverse character and reinvest in this precious resource for future generations.

[Read more](https://cornwall-landscape.org/cornwall-national-landscape-priorities/priority-place/)

![Nature](https://cornwall-landscape.org/wp-content/themes/aonb/resources/images/nature.svg)

### Nature

Set against a backdrop of unprecedented concern for the future of the natural world and ecological crisis the current global response to the effects of human impact on nature is insufficient. The ‘richest’ sites for wildlife are too few, too small, too degraded and too disconnected. Nature Recovery must take place to restore and reverse this ecological decline.

[Read more](https://cornwall-landscape.org/cornwall-national-landscape-priorities/priority-nature/)

![Climate](https://cornwall-landscape.org/wp-content/themes/aonb/resources/images/climate.svg)

### Climate

The climate emergency is the defining challenge of our time. In January 2019, Cornwall Council declared a climate emergency, recognising the need for urgent action to address the climate crisis. Climate change also poses threats to Cornwall National Landscape’s cultural heritage and heritage assets, including historic landscape and seascape.

[Read more](https://cornwall-landscape.org/cornwall-national-landscape-priorities/priority-climate/)
